title: docs: two positioning pages under Core Concepts — 'How ObjectStack compares' and 'When to use ObjectStack, and when not to' — linked from the ontology page and the concepts index
body:
立卡门类别 ③ — 维护者直派的任务 (maintainer-directed task).

## Maintainer ruling (verbatim, untranslated)

> 官网对比页和场景页开卡派发

> 官网不做中文版，中文版有单独的项目 www.objectos.ai

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_011hRnra93sK5Q2gTYYTbdJR on 2026-10-08. The pages are English only; Chinese readers are served by objectos.ai, which this card does not touch.

## Why

The docs site states what the ontology is (concepts/ontology, landed by #21586) and argues it (the blog essay, #21838), but a visitor who arrives asking "how is this different from Palantir, from a semantic layer, from low-code" or "is this for me" finds no page that answers either. Those are the two questions the project's positioning work keeps meeting, and the two searches ("palantir alternative", "ontology for AI agents", "when to use") that currently land nowhere on objectstack.ai. This card adds one page for each, as hand-written docs in the Core Concepts section.

## Part A. content/docs/concepts/compare.mdx — How ObjectStack compares

Audience: a technical reader deciding what kind of thing this is. Tone: the README's, factual, specific, no superlatives. Structure:

1. One paragraph: the word "ontology" is used for four different kinds of thing in 2026, and ObjectStack is a fifth. Point back to concepts/ontology for the definition.
2. One section per kind, each with what it is, what it is good at, and the one difference from ObjectStack:
   - Knowledge ontologies (OWL, RDF, Protégé and the standards built with them): describe a domain and reason over it; not an application and never executed. Difference: ObjectStack's ontology has no axioms or reasoner; it is validated and run.
   - Semantic and context layers over existing data (the category Microsoft Fabric IQ Ontology, Databricks Genie and Unity Catalog metrics, Snowflake semantic views, AWS Context and Google Cloud Knowledge Catalog occupy; in open source, metric semantic layers and agent memory graphs): make data that lives elsewhere legible to agents; read-mostly. Difference: the system of record stays where it was; ObjectStack's ontology is the system.
   - Operational ontologies over existing systems (Palantir Ontology is the reference; open-source reference implementations of the same pattern exist): objects, links, actions and permissions with write-back to source systems. Difference: still a layer over systems that live elsewhere, and in Palantir's case proprietary; ObjectStack generates the database, API, UI and MCP tools from the definition and is Apache-2.0.
   - Metadata-driven application platforms (Salesforce's metadata is the ancestor; open-source cousins include Frappe/ERPNext, Odoo, NocoBase, Payload CMS and Twenty): the closest relatives, metadata that generates tables, APIs and UI, most of which added MCP servers in 2025 and 2026. Difference: their metadata is configuration held in a database and authored in a UI; ObjectStack's is typed TypeScript in the user's repository, validated by a gate, versioned and reviewed as code, written for an AI to author.
   - AI code generation (an agent writes a conventional codebase): no runtime ceiling. Difference: the output is still code, which grows, drifts and cannot be held whole; the gate that rejects a wrong definition at authoring time has no equivalent.
3. A comparison table, rows = the five kinds plus ObjectStack, columns = executable, AI-writable, agent-operable, you own it, is the system itself. Cell values are short words, not ticks.
4. "Where the others are stronger", mandatory and honest: existing data and legacy systems (semantic and operational layers), reasoning over heterogeneous data (knowledge ontologies), algorithm-heavy or unusual UI (code), ecosystem maturity and integrations (the metadata platforms). This section is what makes the page credible; do not soften it.
5. Close with the four-promise sentence and links to concepts/ontology and the blog essay.

Rules for naming others: use public product names as their vendors spell them; state only what their public documentation says, in present tense, hedged with "as of late 2026" where status is changing (Fabric IQ Ontology was in preview in September 2026); no star counts, no market claims, no analyst or consulting-firm quotes, no "the only" or "the first" claims about ObjectStack; describe categories first and name products as examples. Where unsure of a vendor fact, drop the fact rather than guess.

## Part B. content/docs/concepts/when-to-use.mdx — When to use ObjectStack, and when not to

Audience: a reader deciding whether to start. Structure:

1. "A good fit": new business applications (CRM, ticketing, approvals, operations and internal tools), teams small enough that one person or a few can define the business, ISVs shipping many vertical apps, the long tail of departmental apps around a core ERP that live in spreadsheets and low-code today, back offices meant to be operated by agents from day one.
2. "Not a fit today": replacing the core ERP or finance system of a large enterprise; workloads whose value is in integrating many existing systems (external datasources are early and read-only, link to the datasource docs); analytics over data lakes; algorithm-heavy domains such as pricing or scheduling, unless the algorithm is wrapped as an action; workloads that require a certified platform.
3. "Five questions before you start": what we have, how it relates, what can be done, who may do it, what happens when. If the team can answer them, the ontology is a day's work; if it cannot, no tool helps yet. State plainly that the first investment is answering these, not installing anything.
4. "What you get and when": in the first weeks (one definition instead of four copies, apps in days, agents connected by default under the same permissions), after a year (the ontology as an asset in your repository, model-independent, changes gated), later (operations that scale without headcount, cheap experiments, cheap replication across entities). No numbers that are not measured in this repository; the one measured number allowed is the example CRM's size as the ontology page states it.
5. Links: Try it (quick-start), the examples page, concepts/ontology, compare.

## Part C. Wiring

- content/docs/concepts/meta.json: add "compare" and "when-to-use" after "ontology".
- content/docs/concepts/ontology.mdx: one sentence at the end of "What it is not" pointing to compare; one sentence at the end of the page pointing to when-to-use. Nothing else on that page changes.
- content/docs/concepts/index.mdx: the paragraph around line 97 that introduces the ontology gains one sentence naming both pages.
- scripts/docs-audit/handwritten-docs.json: regenerate with the generator named in the file's own header (check-audit-scope --write); never hand-edit.
- Frontmatter on both pages: title, navTitle, description (a real snippet, 110 to 160 characters, see #12238 for why).

## Guardrails for the author

- Docs only: content/docs/concepts/** and the ledger above. No packages/**, no apps/docs/**, no content/blog/**, no README.md (#22232 is in flight on it), no content/docs/references/** (generated), no content/docs/releases/** (release-owned), no CHANGELOG.md, no binaries.
- English only. No model identifiers anywhere.
- Every claim about ObjectStack must be true of main today; check the datasource and MCP docs before stating what federation and agent access do. Every claim about another product must be traceable to that product's public documentation; when it is not, remove the claim.
- The docs build and the doc gates stay green; derive the gate list with scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs from the real change set. check:docs-audit-scope will demand the ledger regeneration; run the generator, do not edit the JSON by hand.
- Changeset: nothing publishes; skip-changeset once packages/** is confirmed untouched.
- Serial constraint: no open PR touches content/docs/concepts at the filing; #22224 and #22232 touch README.md only, which this card does not.

## Non-goals

- Chinese versions (objectos.ai is the Chinese project).
- Changes to the home page, the blog essay, or the README.
- A pricing or "vs" marketing page outside the docs tree.

## Who acts

domain:devx lane, this seat, one os-dev dispatch at the default tier, one docs-only draft PR. Base is origin/main at 3ae59661dc. Precedent on the same section: #21586 via PR #21591 added concepts/ontology.mdx and registered it in the ledger.

## Duplicate check (2026-10-08, open and closed)

- Query "comparison page Palantir semantic layer low-code compare docs": 0 hits.
- Query "use cases OR when to use OR scenarios page docs fit": 211 hits by OR semantics; the ten most relevant are #22232 (the README GIF card, in flight, different files), two seat and patrol pins, #5930, #22079, #20289, #12238 (thin meta descriptions, closed; its rule is applied in Part C), #21876, #21838 (the blog, closed), #20749.
